assumptions: x is representable and s is a nearest representable value to x+y.
The two exact subtraction results s-x and y-t are representable.
t and e are nearest representable values to those exact subtraction results.

formal_statement.lean_header: theorem p12_t2_fast_two_sum_exact (representable : Real -> Prop) (x y : Real) (tr : P12FastTwoSumTrace) ... : tr.s + tr.e = x+y and abs (tr.s-(x+y)) <= abs y
formal_statement.plain_language: A nearest-addition FastTwoSum trace whose two exact subtraction results are representable returns an exact two-term transform and satisfies the local sum-error bound.

informal_proof: Nearest rounding fixes each representable subtraction result, so t=s-x and e=y-t. Substitute both equalities, simplify s+e, and choose x in the nearest-addition relation for the error bound.
informal_statement: Theorem 2's error-free identity (3), with the two representability obligations used in its proof made explicit, together with equation (10).
